lines_cleared: The leaves came down, stranger. Nine years of them, red and gold, and now the Tree flowers from roots to crown.
Hearthroot owes you its water and its fields. I was wrong about strangers. Every door in my town is yours.
king.name: Reeve Aldous
lines: A stranger. We have had no strangers since the leaves stopped falling, and we were glad of it.
The springs that fed the Ylden have stopped. Our fountain is dust, our fields have had no leaf-mould in nine years, and the dwarves under the roots have gone wrong.
My grandmother said a stranger comes before the Fall. I say a stranger is one more mouth.
Take this purse: 1,500 gold. Arm yourself, and if you will not leave, then go down into the Heartwood and find out why its spring is silent.
lines_after: The Heartwood lies past the east gate. Let the Ringreader read you first.
If the spring flows again, Hearthroot will know. The fountain will tell us.

ringreader.name: Ringreader
ringreader.greeting: Rest, wanderer. Let me read your ring into the wood, or teach your body what your mind already knows.
ringreader.greeting_leaf: A leaf of the Ylden, turned to glass. Its grain shows me the Heartwood Spring, stopped by a dam of stillglass. Go down, wanderer. Rest here when you need to.

townsfolk_well.name: Old Wena
lines: Forty years I drew water from that fountain. Now I draw dust.
My grandson went into the roots to look for the spring. He said the sap was moving. Sap doesn't move.

lines_cleared: Petals in the fountain! I spent the morning fishing them out, and then I gave up and let them float.
My grandson says it is the same all the way up. Pink to the crown. He wants to climb it. I said: after supper.
townsfolk_well_glad.name: Old Wena
lines: Full! Forty years, and I never saw it brim like this. Listen to it.
My grandson came home this morning, soaked to the skin and laughing. He says the rain up top has stopped.

lines_cleared: Three days of music, the Elder said. Then the leaves fell, and the Tree flowered, and nobody wants to stop.
I've a new tune for the Leaffall. No name yet. They keep asking for the one about the stranger who climbed the Tree, and I keep playing this one.
festival_piper.name: Festival Piper
lines: Hearthroot hasn't danced since the leaves stopped falling. Three springs running, three days of music, the Elder says.
They say the dwarves of Vorrhallow still sleep under the water. Somebody ought to wake them. Not me, mind. I pipe.

lines_cleared: The Hollows are quiet now, near enough. A few blinkhops still hop about. Old habits.
Mind, the beasts down there never were the Everbloom's. They were the Tree's all along. Watch the eye, same as ever.
townsfolk_gate.name: Gate Watch
lines: East gate leads down into the Heartwood. Blinkhops hop about near the entrance. Watch the eye: it flashes before it jumps.
The rot dwarves carry shields. Get behind them, or wait for the swing and hit back.

amberlee_widow.name: Hesk
lines: Amberlee, they called it. The town in the hollow. Now it's me and the Ringreader and the drip of the sap.
When the spring went quiet the sap started to crawl. It filled the lanes in a night. The others ran for Hearthroot.
If you mean to go deeper, the shrine below keeps you safe. Past it, a shaft climbs east to the dwarves' old hall.

lines_cleared: Blossom down the well-shaft! It comes through every crack in the trunk. Amberlee smells of honey.
Brannoc says he'll sell nothing but garlands now. Tilde says he won't last the week.
amberlee_widow_glad.name: Hesk
lines: The sap went hard as glass in an hour. You did that, didn't you?
Brannoc and Tilde came back the next morning. Shops open, lamps lit. It almost feels like a town.

lines_cleared: The light's gone out of the crown. Not the sun: the other one. The glass's.
We'll dig the old galleries again. Honest stone, no glass in it. You'll find us down there.
amberlee_miner.name: Dwarf Orrin
lines: You want to know who did this? We did. The Hollin. Our Thane gave the word, and we dug the glass for him and sang while we did it.
Those of us who kept away from the glass kept our heads. The Hollin Tower is ours, or was. Durgan holds it now. Bring a Delver's Pick if you go: the old walls only crack for one.

lines_cleared: The water has gone, and the light from the crown has gone with it. Vorrhallow wakes under an honest sky.
We buried the king on the dais where he fell. You may visit him. He would have wanted to thank you himself.
vorrhallow_steward.name: Steward Hrafna
lines: The water is going down. I can hear it in the stair, running away below, for the first time since the king set his flower in the glass.
He could not bear to lose one more thing, so he let nothing go. It kept us, after a fashion: asleep under the flood. You have let him weep at last, and us wake.
His seed is yours. The gate of the Evercrown is up the Glass Rise, east of here. And below us, under the last stone, the Sunken Spring still holds its water. Let it lie, for now.

lines_cleared: Dry stone! I've not laid a course on dry stone in three years.
The crystal in the walls has gone grey and soft as chalk. We chip it out by the bucket. The masonry under it is sound.
vorrhallow_mason.name: Mason Brokk
lines: Woke on my back in the market with weed in my beard. The tide line's a foot lower already.
We'll have the lower city dry by spring. Mind the water-clocks, though: they still hold their hour.

lines_cleared: Vorrund wept at the last, they say, and the flower he planted is dead. Kettleforge can mourn him now, as a king, and her with him.
The forge burns day and night. Hrothgar says the dead glass folds into steel better than anything he's struck. A last gift, he calls it. I call it a warning.
kettleforge_elder.name: Elder Basalt
lines: You freed him. Durgan, our champion. The Thane bolted him into that engine to guard the glassworks, and the glass kept him there.
Nine years ago the Withering took our queen. Our king, Vorrund, would not mourn her. He went up to the crown with his grafting blade instead.
He has not come back as himself. Take the Sun Seed, elf. It was the summer Durgan carried, and the gate of the Evercrown will know it.

lines_cleared: Three years in the deep galleries, and now I can't stay out of the sun.
Have you seen the crown from the Lookout? All flowers. The dwarves of Kettleforge never thought to look up.
kettleforge_miner.name: Dwarf Tamsin
lines: Three years we hid in the deep galleries while that drill chewed the halls.
The lift runs again. Ride it down to the Tower Foot and you'll be back in the Heartwood in a breath.

lines_cleared: Hrothgar's still at the anvil. Bring him a Stillglass Shard and he'll beat it into your blade. Best steel in the Tree, he says.
Up the trunk the mist is thin as breath now. I went up and came back dry. First dwarf in three years.
kettleforge_digger.name: Dwarf Okko
lines: Hrothgar's forge is lit! Bring him your blade. He'll fold it twice if your purse is heavy enough.
Up the trunk the mist begins. Nobody who went into it came back dry.

kettleforge_physician.name: Physician Halvar
lines: Nothing ails you that I can see. Good. My cots have held enough of the drill's work.
Come back bleeding, elf, or green with a bog's poison. You will not pay a coin in Kettleforge.
lines_treated: Hold still. Moss for the cuts, ash-salt for the poison, and a dwarf's own tonic for the rest.
There. Whole again, and not a coin. Kettleforge does not charge the one who silenced the drill.
lines_cleared: My cots are empty for the first time in three years. I have taken up the harp. Badly.
Still, if the climb opens you up, come here first. Old habits.

vorrhallow_houndkeeper.name: Houndkeeper Brand
lines: I wound the king's hounds, every morning, for forty years. Brass hearts, iron jaws, a key in each back.
The first of them, the Alpha, never wound down. It's still in its den under the kennels, guarding the chest the king left it.
lines_cleared: I melted the last of the hound-keys into a bell for the market. It rings on the hour. Nobody needs winding.
The kennels are a garden now. Brass flowers, the children call them. They're gears. I let them think what they like.

vorrhallow_houndkeeper_glad.name: Houndkeeper Brand
lines: So the Alpha's spring is spent. Forty years I heard it pacing under the floor. Tonight I'll sleep.
The king locked a Life Fruit in its chest for his first hound. If it grows in you now, elf, then it went to someone who earned it.
lines_cleared: I melted the last of the hound-keys into a bell for the market. It rings on the hour. Nobody needs winding.
The kennels are a garden now. Brass flowers, the children call them. They're gears. I let them think what they like.
The crown-leaf bears flowers again, not one Devouring Bloom. White and pink, as far as the eye goes.
Some of us wanted the summer to last forever. I was one. Our wardens stand at the bridge out of habit now. Rest with us, elf.
sylvarre_elder.name: Elder Aelwen
lines: A stranger, climbing the Tree from the roots? Then the springs below run again. We felt the sap stir, and not all of us were glad.
Above us, on the crown-leaf, a flower took root the year the leaves stopped falling. We call it Snapcrown, the Devouring Bloom. It eats the light, and those who go to look at it.
Our wardens crossed the sky-gaps with the Elven Stride. Its shrine is in the Windloft, up the north bough. If you mean to face the Bloom, go there first.

lines_cleared: Still here, still watching. Somebody has to. The mantises haven't heard the news.
The petals fall all day. Hard to see a leaf mantis in a blossom storm. Keep your blade out, same as before.
sylvarre_warden.name: Warden Faelan
lines: Hold. You came over the bridge? Past the mantises? Then keep your blade out, elf. You've earned it.
The north bough climbs to the crown-leaf. Nobody goes up there now. The last warden who tried, the Bloom swallowed whole.

sylvarre_squire.name: Squire Ithil
lines: Past this door is the Thorn Yard. The first knight the Tree ever grew still keeps it, and he keeps it from us.
We call him the Captain. His bark turns a blade like a shield. My father swore that fire was the only thing it feared.
lines_cleared: The Thorn Yard is all briar-roses now. I go in to sit where the Captain stood. It feels like the right thing.
Fire was the answer, my father said. He never saw how it ended. I tell him about it anyway.

sylvarre_squire_glad.name: Squire Ithil
lines: The Captain is down? Then the Thorn Yard is ours again, after all these years. I went in. It's quiet. Too quiet.
He wasn't cruel, you know. He just never stopped guarding. The Tree grew him to keep a door, and he kept it.
lines_cleared: The Thorn Yard is all briar-roses now. I go in to sit where the Captain stood. It feels like the right thing.
Fire was the answer, my father said. He never saw how it ended. I tell him about it anyway.

polesend_reedcutter.name: Reedcutter Siobhe
lines: Don't go through the east door. The Matriarch lives in the mire past it, the mother of every hag in this fog.
When she raises her staff the bog lights up around your feet. Stand still and the mud takes you. My brother learned that.
Hit her while she's casting, he said. It breaks the spell and she drops her staff. He was right. It didn't save him.
lines_cleared: The mire is only a mire now. I cut reeds where she stood, and nothing reaches up out of the mud for my ankles.
Every hag in the fog was her daughter, they say. The fog is thinning. Perhaps they have all gone home to her.

polesend_reedcutter_glad.name: Reedcutter Siobhe
lines: The Matriarch is sunk for good? Then I can cut reeds in the east mire again, for the first time since I was a girl.
My brother would have laughed to hear it. He always said she'd drop that staff for anyone quick enough.
lines_cleared: The mire is only a mire now. I cut reeds where she stood, and nothing reaches up out of the mud for my ankles.
Every hag in the fog was her daughter, they say. The fog is thinning. Perhaps they have all gone home to her.
Petal-silk! The blossom spins finer than the leaves ever did. Pink, if you like that sort of thing.
The dwarves climbed up yesterday with iron to trade. Real dwarves, with beards and bad jokes. I'd forgotten how much I missed them.
sylvarre_weaver.name: Weaver Imra
lines: Leaf-silk, spun in the sun. It won't stop a blade, but it keeps the wind off.
The dwarves used to climb up to trade iron for silk. Then the Everbloom came, and the dwarves stopped climbing, and some stopped being dwarves.

lines_cleared: The rods sing again and the bells ring on their own. No storm needed: the Tree's light runs down the copper now.
Carillon will cast you a bell, hero. Your name on it. It is the least we can do, and the loudest.
spires_mayor.name: Mayor Halloran
lines: You crossed the fallen bridge? Then the Bloom is dead, and the wind brought us a hero. Welcome to Carillon.
Our bells and lifts ran on the storm. Lightning came down the rods and the copper sang. Then a great bird came out of the clouds and the conduits went cold.
Skyrend, we call it. It nests in the Spires above the town. Nothing that flies is safe, and nothing that climbs.
Our oldest bell names the year of the Withering, and the one who swore it would be the last loss: Thane Vorrund, who planted the flower.

lines_cleared: Forty years I rang the bells by hand. This morning they rang themselves, the whole peal, for an hour.
I sat on the step and listened. Bramble's still in the old cellar, mind. Some things the flowers don't fix.
spires_bellkeeper.name: Old Bellkeeper Rusk
lines: The old bell cellar? Bramble choked it the year the storm turned. Blades only snag in that stuff.
Ysolde sells a scroll of Emberfall. Dry bramble goes up like tinder. I'd do it myself, but I'm too old to aim.

lines_cleared: The mire gave up its men this morning. They walked out of the water dry, sat on the boardwalk, and asked for bread.
Garrick does not remember the stair, nor the stone, nor me at first. He remembers the road home. That is enough.
lampwick_widow.name: Marta
lines: My Garrick was a miner. When the Everbloom took root, the dwarf king paid gold for every cart of its glass, and Lampwick's men went down the drowned stair to dig.
They came back up wet to the bone and would not speak. Then they went back down, and the water closed over them. You have seen them in the mire.
If you strike one down, be quick. Whatever is left of him in there, I hope it is tired.

lines_cleared: Sun on the boardwalks! Real sun, not lamp-light. I stood in it so long my neck burned.
I will keep lighting the lamps, mind. Habit. If the fog ever comes back, I will be ready.
lampwick_lamplighter.name: Lamplighter Nell
lines: Mind the dark between the lamps. Lampwick was built on the boardwalks before the fog came, and the fog never left.
I light every lamp at dusk and again at dawn. You cannot tell them apart in here, so I light them twice to be sure.
East is the Feather Hollow, where the elves' messengers roosted. A pair of winged boots still sits on the perch. No one here can reach it.

lines_cleared: The black water's gone clear. I can see the old road under it, every stone, all the way to the Tower.
I've a mind to pole a barge again. Bread down to Kettleforge, flowers back. Will you ride with me, one day?
polesend_ferryman.name: Old Teague the Poler
lines: Forty years I poled the dwarf king's barges down this road. Ore from the deep cuts, bread back up. A fair trade, till the Everbloom.
Then the king wanted only the glass, and the barges came back empty but for his men. Quiet men. Wet men.
The spring's back, so the boardwalks are back. Lampwick lies west beyond the Lantern Landing, if you are going visiting.

lines_cleared: The Tree blooms, and my spring still sleeps. Two of three will do, they say. Clear the spout anyway, for an old dwarf.
heartwood_keeper.name: Odran
lines: I keep the Heartwood Spring, as my father did. Every spring has its keeper. That was the old way.
My father swore it took an Amber Draught to wake a spring. It doesn't. It takes someone to clear the spout. I'm too old to go in.

lines_cleared: The Tree drinks from all three now. I sit here and listen to it. A keeper's work is mostly listening.
heartwood_keeper_glad.name: Odran
lines: Hear that? First water in the trunk since the glass dammed it. It'll be in Hearthroot's fountain by dark.
There are two more springs, higher up, and two more keepers waiting at them. Tell them Odran sent you.

lines_cleared: The Tree blooms even with my spring choked. Clear it all the same. The fog has no right to it.
haar_keeper.name: Ilka
lines: You beat the thing that coiled round it. Its breath was the fog, you know — it boiled the tanks dry and the steam settled over the whole marsh. I watched from the cistern stair for a year.
I keep the Haar Spring. The tanks are full again, but the spout is still choked with bone. Clear it.

lines_cleared: Three springs, three keepers, and a Tree in bloom. Odran owes me a drink.
haar_keeper_glad.name: Ilka
lines: There. Its steam has gone cold at last, and the fog with it — Lampwick will see its own boardwalks by morning.
One spring left, up in the sky where the elves drew the rain. Its keeper is a sleeper. Be patient.

lines_cleared: Petals on the wind, and still my spring is dry. Clear it, and I'll go back to sleeping in the rain.
sky_keeper.name: Arel
lines: Mm? Oh. A visitor. Forgive me. With the roc on the spring there was nothing to keep, so I slept.
I keep the Sky Spring. The roc is gone, so clear the spring and the rain will run to the Tree again.

lines_cleared: The rain falls soft now. I've a mind to stay awake for it.
sky_keeper_glad.name: Arel
lines: Water on my face. That woke me better than you did. The storm is breaking.
Below us, under the clouds, lies Vorrhallow, the dwarf king's city. No rain has reached it in years.

polesend_barmaid.name: Barmaid Brigid
lines: Sit, dry your boots. Every barge-hand who comes through the Black Water tells me something, and I tell the next one for free.
The Matriarch took an Acorn Charm off a drowned knight. It lies in the far corner of her mire, past our east door, where no one looks. Wear it and your blade bites a little deeper.
The Haar Wyrm lies coiled round the Haar Spring, past the Dry Cistern. Nobody in Polesend has tasted that water since it came.
lines_cleared: The spring runs, the fog's lifting, and the bargemen drink to you every night. I've stopped charging them for it.
Someone has to keep the lamps lit in here. It may as well be me, and it may as well be forever.

polesend_drinker.name: Old Cormac
lines: I poled the king's ore barges forty years. Ask me anything. I'll answer something.
Lampwick's elves sent their letters by wing. One messenger left her boots on the perch at Feather Hollow, by Lampwick. Wear them and the air holds a second step for you.
The Sunken Chapel, down the Marsh Road. The dwarves drowned in it kept lanterns burning on the altar. Don't go to pray.
lines_cleared: The water went down and took forty years of my stories with it. Now I have to make new ones up.
Barges again, by spring. I'll pole the first one myself, if Brigid doesn't hide my hat.
